results.title: How Telegram runs with only 40 employees | Pavel Durov and Lex Fridman
results.author: Lex Clips
highlights:
- All right, we took a break, and now we're
back. I gotta ask you about Telegram, the company. I got to meet some of the
brilliant engineers that work there. Telegram runs lean. Relative
to other technology companies that achieve the scale that
Telegram does, it has very few employees. So how many people are on the core team,
let's say the core engineering team? - The core engineering team is
about 40 people. This includes backend, frontend designers,
system administrators. - Can you speak to the philosophy behind
running a company with so few employees? - Well, what we realized
really early is that quantity of employees doesn't translate
to quality of the product they produce. In many cases, it's the opposite. If you have too many people, they have
to coordinate their efforts, constantly communicate, and 90% of
their time will be spent on coordinating the small pieces of work
they're responsible for between each other. The other problem with having
too many employees is that some of them won't get
enough work to do. And if they don't get enough work to do, they
demotivate everybody else by their mere existence. They're still there,
they're still getting the salary, but they don't do
anything. And if they don't do anything, more often than not,
they will start trying to find their purpose elsewhere,
maybe inside your team, but not by doing productive work, but
by finding problems that don't exist within the team. And that
can disrupt the team and the mood inside it even
further. Also, when you intentionally don't allow
some of your team members to hire more people to help them, they
will be forced to automate things. In our case, you know, we have tens of thousands of servers around the
world, almost 100,000, distributed across several continents and data centers.
If you try to manage this system manually without automation, you will probably end up hiring thousands
of people, tens of thousands of people. But if you rely on algorithms
and the team is forced to put together algorithms in order to
manage it, then it becomes much more scalable, and much more efficient, and
interestingly, much more reliable as well. - And more resilient to the
changing geopolitics, to the changing technology, all of
that. Because if you automate the distributed aspect of
the data storage and all the compute, then that's going to be resilient

results.title: Telegram says it has 'about 30 engineers'; security experts say that's a red flag | TechCrunch
results.author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai
highlights:
Over the weekend, a clip from a recent interview with Telegram’s founder Pavel Durov went semi-viral on X (previously Twitter). In the video, Durov tells right-wing personality Tucker Carlson that he is the only product manager at the company, and that he only employs “about 30 engineers.”

...

“What makes Telegram different (and much worse!) is that Telegram is not just a messaging app, it is also a social media platform. As a social media platform, it is sitting on an enormous amount of user data. Indeed, it is sitting on the contents of all communications that are not one-on-one messages that have been specifically [end-to-end] encrypted,” Galperin told TechCrunch. “‘Thirty engineers’ means that there is no one to fight legal requests, there is no infrastructure for dealing with abuse and content moderation issues.”

“And I would even argue that the quality of those 30 engineers isn’t that great,” Galperin continued. “Also, if I was a threat actor, I would definitely consider this to be encouraging news. Every attacker loves a profoundly understaffed and overworked opponent.”

...

Telegram’s spokesperson confirmed the company has 30 developers working on the apps and infrastructure, but claims to have an additional 30 people on its “core team.” The spokesperson did not answer our specific questions, including whether the company has a chief security officer, and how many of its engineers work full time on securing the platform.

...

"I still come up with most of the features, I still work directly with every engineer, every designer who is implementing these features."

...

...

# В Telegram раскритиковали заявления экспертов по безопасности TechCrunch по поводу 30 инженеров и серверов в ОАЭ

25 июня 2024 года представитель Telegram прокомментировал ресурсу «Код Дурова» материал издания TechCrunch с заявлением экспертов по безопасности по поводу всего 30 инженеров и серверов в ОАЭ. Он пояснил, что материал TechCrunch основан на непонимании слов Дурова в разговоре с Такером, а на самом деле основная команда мессенджера около 60 человек, не включая отдельные команды по модерации. Да, команда инженеров небольшая, это сделано намеренно. Также у мессенджера при этом нет серверов в ОАЭ.

Ответ представителя Telegram:

> — Во-первых, в материале издания была допущена откровенная ошибка: у Telegram нет никаких серверов в ОАЭ. Представитель мессенджера подчеркнул, что никакие данные пользователей там не хранятся. 
> 
> — Во-вторых, материал TechCrunch во многом основан на непонимании того, что имел в виду Павел Дуров, рассказывая про сотрудников в интервью Карлсону Такеру.
> 
> — В-третьих, на самом деле за разработку и инфраструктуру отвечают 30 человек, но основная команда при этом состоит примерно из 60 человек:
> 
> — Помимо этих 60 членов основной команды, в Telegram есть отдельные команды по модерации и борьбе со злоупотреблениями, — подчеркнул представитель мессенджера в комментарии «Коду Дурова».

 Представитель Telegram объяснил, что команда разработчиков у сервиса небольшая намеренно, но она включает в себе экспертов в своих областях — это помогает быстрее реагировать на ситуации, чем в компаниях с большими командами.

results.title: How Telegram runs a $30 billion platform with just 30 team members | - The Times of India
results.author: TOI Tech Desk
highlights:
Telegram, valued at $30 billion with over 1 billion users, remarkably operates with only 30 employees. This lean structure is enabled by automation, remote work, and a flat hierarchy. Founded on privacy principles, Telegram's custom protocols and decentralized network support its global reach, attracting users in censorship-heavy regions. The company's unique recruitment and subscription model contribute to its success.

...

In an era where tech companies typically thrive on massive teams, sprawling campuses, and layers of management, Telegram stands as a striking anomaly. As of March 2025, Telegram valued at $30 billion and boasts over 1 billion active users—yet it operates with a core team of just 30 people. This minimalist approach has captivated the attention of business leaders, entrepreneurs, and organizational strategists across the globe. How did a platform founded just over a decade ago manage to scale to global prominence without the conventional resources that most Silicon Valley giants deem essential? Here's the origin, operational structure, technological innovations, and strategic choices that have enabled Telegram to reach such staggering heights with astonishing efficiency.

## How Telegram runs a $30 billion platform with just 30 team members

Telegram’s most astonishing feat lies not just in its user base or valuation but in its operating model. Unlike competitors like WhatsApp (Meta) or Signal, which employ thousands, Telegram runs its operations with approximately 30 employees. Founder Pavel Durov acts as the sole product manager. The company operates without traditional HR departments or corporate hierarchies. This ultra-lean structure is sustained by three core pillars:

- Automation-driven processes: Many backend tasks—like customer support, server maintenance, and content moderation—are handled by intelligent bots and automated systems.
- Remote work model: Employees work remotely from various parts of the world, eliminating overhead costs related to physical infrastructure.
- Flat organizational structure: Direct communication between Durov and his engineers eliminates delays and enhances decision-making efficiency.

results.title: Telegram: 1 Billion Users, 30 Engineers. No HR, No LinkedIn ...
results.author: Gabriela Quintela
highlights:
Much about Telegram is wrapped in mystery, and the company has not disclosed its exact staff size. In 2023, Fortune reported a company spokesperson saying Telegram had “an agile core team of around 60.” Its CEO, Pavel Durov, has said the engineering team is closer to 30. 

Telegram’s LinkedIn page keeps the mystery: “Telegram has a ‘No LinkedIn’ policy,” it states, adding that individuals claiming to be past or current employees never worked at Telegram.

Valued at USD 30 billion, the company doesn’t seem to have a traditional office — though it does have an operational base in Dubai.

# Super efficiency 

In 2024, Pavel Durov told journalist Tucker Carlson that he employed only “about 30 engineers” to run his platform. He did not disclose the full size of Telegram’s team — what he did say was that he has no HR department, spends no money on marketing, and that he was still the only product manager.

“I think that having myself as the sole owner, director, and product manager for this extensive period of time and the company’s development allowed us to move faster,” he declared. “I still come up with most of the features; I still work directly with every engineer, every designer who is implementing these features. I’m running this company because I enjoy it. I’m the only product manager because I think this is the way I can contribute.” 

When asked how big his HR department was, he replied: “Zero. Well, you could say it’s me.” 

“We, in a way, decentralized that [the hiring process],” he explained. “We started a platform where we host contests for engineers — it’s actually contest.com, we have the separate platform for that — and we select the best of the best engineers as a result of the competitions that we organize; we hold them every month or two months. So, after a series of these competitions, we select the best of the best of the best, and then they maybe could join our team, which is just about 30 engineers. So, it’s really compact, the team, super efficient. It’s like a Navy SEAL team. This is how we operate; we don’t need an HR department to find super talented engineers.”
